items.title: Parse and preserve Authority runner provider declaration as host-neutral metadata
items.context: Read LATTICE_AUTHORITY_RUNNER_PROVIDER or equivalent runner config without constraining Authority identity to fake/codex/claude only. Known aliases may still map to execution adapters separately. Happy path: codex-cli or claude-code is accepted and emitted as runner/provider metadata. Edge: missing declaration preserves legacy behavior. Adversarial: custom declaration does not bypass API key, actor key, signature, lease, or server policy checks.
items.userSees: authority_status / authority_enforce_runner shows runnerProvider=codex-cli or antigravity with runnerProviderValid=true instead of a local unsupported-provider warning.

happy.desc: LATTICE_AUTHORITY_RUNNER_PROVIDER=codex-cli or antigravity normalizes to the same declaration string and is reported valid.

edge.desc: Missing runner provider still defaults to codex and claude / CLAUDE_CODE aliases still normalize to claude-code.

adversarial.desc: A custom provider declaration is not treated as authorization proof and does not set productionDone, receiptVerified, or authorityReady by itself.

items.title: Propagate provider declaration through register, heartbeat, SSE watch, claim, and takeover diagnostics
items.context: Ensure the same declaration used by the runner is visible to Authority calls and troubleshooting output, while signed claim remains the ownership boundary. Server rejection should be reported as server policy rejection, not as a local enum parse failure.
items.userSees: authority_enforce_runner --dry-run and live runner diagnostics carry the declared provider through register, heartbeat, jobs stream hint, and signed claim planning; server rejection remains visible as server-side failure, not local enum failure.

happy.desc: Declared provider metadata is sent consistently in actor key registration, runner registration, heartbeat, and signed claim payloads.

edge.desc: authority_job_create accepts a non-enum provider string locally and leaves accept/reject to the server response.

adversarial.desc: SSE jobs.available never grants ownership without the normal signed claim accepted by the server.

items.title: Add focused regression tests for non-enum Authority provider declarations
items.context: Cover arbitrary provider declaration acceptance and propagation for Authority flows without expanding product scope or hardcoding a new exhaustive host list. Existing codex, claude, fake, and Antigravity-related behavior should remain compatible where those adapters are expected.
items.userSees: Focused smoke tests pass with custom provider declarations, existing codex/claude compatibility, and fail-closed authorization boundaries.

happy.desc: Focused smokes prove arbitrary provider declarations are accepted and propagated by CLI Authority flows.

edge.desc: Existing codex default, claude alias, and Antigravity-adjacent behavior remain compatible.

adversarial.desc: Regression tests prove declaration acceptance does not bypass credentials, signature, lease, or server-policy checks.
